'''4104''' ('''four thousand one hundred [and] four''') is the [[natural number]] following 4103 and preceding 4105.

== In mathematics ==
4104 is a [[composite number]], as it has the [[prime factorization]] 2<sup>3</sup> × 3<sup>3</sup> × 19.

4104 can be expressed as the sum of two positive [[cubes]] in two different ways: 4104 is the sum of 4096 + 8 (that is, 16<sup>3</sup> + 2<sup>3</sup>), and also the sum of 3375 + 729 (that is, 15<sup>3</sup> + 9<sup>3</sup>).<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Mitesh J. |first1=Mitesh |last2=Ghodasara |first2=G. V. |title=Cube Sum Labeling (Taxi-Cab Labeling) of Graphs |journal=International Journal of Mathematical Combinatorics |date=2023 |volume=2 |pages=78-86 |url=https://www.mathcombin.com/upload/file/20230708/1688786361801023148.pdf |access-date=2026-09-16}}</ref><ref name="A001235">{{cite OEIS|A001235|Taxi-cab numbers: sums of 2 cubes in more than 1 way}}</ref> By the former property, it is also the sum of two powers of 8: 8<sup>4</sup> + 8<sup>1</sup>.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A055259|Sums of two powers of 8}}</ref>

There are 4104 different [[Cayley graph]]s on 26 [[Vertex (graph theory)|node]]s,<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A185959|Number of Cayley graphs on n nodes}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=McKay |first=Brendan D. |last2=Praeger |first2=Cheryl E. |date=February 1994 |title=Vertex-transitive graphs which are not Cayley graphs, I |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/S144678870003473X/type/journal_article |journal=Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society. Series A. Pure Mathematics and Statistics |language=en |volume=56 |issue=1 |pages=53–63 |doi=10.1017/S144678870003473X |issn=0263-6115}}</ref> and 4104 ways of [[Four color theorem|4-coloring]] a [[Map (graph theory)|map]] in which there is a central circle surrounded by a ring divided into 10 regions.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A090860|Number of ways of 4-coloring a map in which there is a central circle surrounded by an annulus divided into n-1 regions. There are n regions in all}}</ref>
